segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: A new era arrived in Hollywood in the 1960s, with new directors who would go on to become landmarks of the craft.
segments.text: A new era arrived in Hollywood in the nineteen sixties, with new directors who would go on to become landmarks of the craft.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: In the 1950s, the old studio system and even the idea that Hollywood was the world center of cinema were toppled. In the following decade, Hollywood - like all of American society - lived through a state of upheaval.
segments.text: In the nineteen fifties, the old studio system and even the idea that Hollywood was the world center of cinema were toppled. In the following decade, Hollywood - like all of American society - lived through a state of upheaval.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: The court-ordered separation of the major studios' production and distribution arms was followed by a proliferation of "runaway productions" - big American productions shot abroad to use box office receipts frozen in countries whose laws required money earned there to be spent there, or to take advantage of resources such as cheaper labor. Even so, the major studios managed to stay afloat as Los Angeles replaced New York as the main center of television production.

segments.original: The idea that a studio should pour most of its resources into one or two blockbusters took several blows during the decade. segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: In the early 1960s, the lists of movie stars were dominated by performers such as Cary Grant, Elizabeth Taylor, Frank Sinatra, and John Wayne. By the end of the decade, the leading names in the film pantheon were Paul Newman, Warren Beatty, Faye Dunaway, Robert Redford, Dustin Hoffman, Sidney Poitier, Jane Fonda, and Barbra Streisand. And it was not just a matter of youth and beauty: Charles Bronson and Lee Marvin, former supporting tough guys, were elevated to leading roles in action films, while the star of the highest-grossing American film of 1966, Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966), was Elizabeth Taylor (1932-2011), an old-guard actress.

segments.original: In New York, John Cassavetes (1929-1989) - who kept up a film acting career to support his work as a writer - was experimenting freely with experimental cinema, while Andy Warhol (1928-1987) turned his cameras on drug addicts, prostitutes, losers, and drag queens to turn them into "superstars". American directors such as Stanley Kubrick (1928-1999) and Richard Lester (b. 1932) preferred to work in Britain, which had experienced its own New Wave. segments.original: One of the most powerful films of the late decade, Midnight Cowboy (1969), directed by fellow foreigner Schlesinger, shed light on America's underclass and the taboo of male prostitution. segments.original: The history of 1960s Hollywood films can also be viewed through the lens of changing censorship standards and sociopolitical attitudes.
